articles.title: Noskova beats Gauff to reach WTA Finals semi-finals as Pegula stays alive
articles.summary: Czech defeats Gauff 6-3, 6-3 to reach last four. Pegula eliminates Kostyuk with straight-sets victory. Gauff and Pegula remain in contention for final berth. Linda Noskova secured her place in the semi-finals of the WTA Finals with a 6-3, 6-3 victory over Coco Gauff on Tuesday, while Jessica Pegula…
body: The Czech, who beat Kostyuk in her opening match, has won both encounters without dropping a set and is assured of advancing to the knockout stage. Gauff and Pegula are both 1-1, with the final round-robin matches on Thursday set to determine who joins Noskova in the last four.
Pegula earlier bounced back from her opening defeat to Gauff with a 6-2, 7-5 victory over Kostyuk, eliminating the Ukrainian from semi-final contention.

The American made a strong start, breaking Kostyuk in the opening game and securing another break to claim the first set. She carried that momentum into the second, breaking again at the start before the pair exchanged breaks twice.
Kostyuk’s mistakes undermined her attempts to fight back, with the Ukrainian committing 17 unforced errors in the opening set compared with Pegula’s three.

articles.title: Izzy Neale, ‘dearly loved’ Australian apprentice jockey, dies after fall at regional track
articles.summary: Twenty-two-year-old suffered severe injuries at race on Sunday. ‘Words are not enough,’ says trainer Richard Freedman. Apprentice jockey Izzy Neale has died following a fall at a regional racecourse.
body: Neale suffered severe injuries when her mount Marnoo fell entering the home straight in the Warren Shire Cotton Cup in NSW.
The 22-year-old fell heavily and was unconscious when airlifted to Dubbo Hospital on Sunday.
On Tuesday night, her family released a statement saying she had not recovered.
“It is with deep sadness and broken hearts that we announce the passing of our beloved Izzy, surrounded by her closest family and friends,” the family said.

articles.title: Noskova dismantles Gauff to reach WTA Finals last four
articles.summary: Linda Noskova became the first player to reach the WTA Finals semi-finals after securing a dominant 6-3 6-3 straight-sets victory over Coco Gauff.
body: It was a commanding display from the Czech against the world No 4, as Noskova made it two wins from two with another impressive performance following her victory over Marta Kostyuk.
The 21-year-old is yet to drop a set at the WTA Finals, underlining her excellent form as she continues to enjoy an outstanding season.
She has now advanced with her two wins, while Gauff and Jessica Pegula sit on one win and one loss in Group One.
After suffering two defeats, Kostyuk has been eliminated from the tournament. The Ukrainian replaced world No 1 Elena Rybakina, who was forced to withdraw due to illness.

articles.title: NFL trade deadline: Kirk Cousins returns to Vikings as Raiders hand starting job to Fernando Mendoza
articles.summary: Minnesota acquire veteran quarterback for 2027 pick. Cousins returns to Vikings after six seasons with team. No 1 pick Mendoza set to make first NFL start. NFL trade deadline 2026 – as it happened. Kirk Cousins is heading back to Minnesota.
body: The Vikings have acquired the veteran quarterback from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a third-round pick in the 2027 draft, according to multiple reports, including from ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport.

The move reunites Cousins with the franchise with which he spent six seasons from 2018 to 2023 and gives Minnesota an experienced option under center as they look to revive their season. The Vikings got off to a 6-0 start to the season thanks to their standout defense, but have lost their last two games. Former No 1 overall pick Kyler Murray had been their starter, but he has been underwhelming in his first season in Minnesota. He missed Monday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills through injury and his replacement, Carson Wentz, threw two interceptions and was lucky to avoid another in a dreadful performance.
After Monday’s loss, Minnesota coach Kevin O’Connell admitted the team was looking at other options.

articles.title: McTominay reveals heart treatment two days before Scotland’s World Cup opener
articles.summary: Midfielder was in hospital before Haiti match. ‘I had to get the shock on my heart,’ says McTominay. Scott McTominay has revealed he was in hospital under sedation to have a “shock on my heart” just 48 hours before Scotland began their World Cup campaign against Haiti in June.
body: At the time McTominay’s absence from training was put down to a stomach complaint. It emerged in August that the Napoli midfielder needed surgery to remedy an irregular heartbeat. The operation took place in September, causing McTominay to miss Scotland’s first four Nations League matches. The player has now said the matter arose in the US as Scotland prepared for their World Cup opener at Boston Stadium.

McTominay is back in the international fold for Scotland’s fixtures against North Macedonia and Switzerland. Talking to media in Glasgow the 29-year-old said: “The World Cup was difficult for me to be honest. I had to go and get the shock on my heart. It was two days before the Haiti game and you have prepared so well. I was in such good condition and then something like that happens. And you think: ‘How is this happening to me?’ But then you have to get on with it.

“These are cards you are dealt in football. Sometimes things don’t go your way and you have to continue to do your best. It’s nowhere near an excuse but it’s something you have to look back on and say it’s part of the process.

articles.title: Pocognoli to lean on Scotland's 'captain group of five'
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli is delighted to welcome "exciting" Scott McTominay into his squad, saying the Napoli midfielder is one of the "fantastic leaders" that helped persuade him to become Scotland head coach.
body: The Belgian revealed the fit-again 29-year-old "is in my captain group of five", who will be relied upon to make sure his instructions are carried out on the field of play.

McTominay missed Pocognoli's first, four-game Uefa Nations League camp in charge as Scotland drew with Slovenia, lost to Switzerland, beat North Macedonia, but then lost the return at home to the Slovenians.
The midfielder, who is back playing after a minor heart procedure, has revealed he received treatment to correct an irregular heartbeat two days before Scotland's World Cup win over Haiti in June.
"I don't have to paint a picture of how important a player he is for us," said Pocognoli as he prepared for Friday's meeting with North Macedonia at Hampden.

articles.title: ‘Why are we associated with conferences anymore?’ SEC coach questions the point of conferences in 24-team playoff
articles.summary: The College Football Playoff is expanding to 24 teams next season, and the change will also mean the end of conference championship games for the Power 4 leagues. Not everyone is on board with that decision. Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz is the latest to push back.
body: On Monday, the CFP and ESPN agreed to a five-year deal worth nearly $1.7 billion that will expand the playoff field to 24 teams starting in 2027. The field will include 19 at-large bids, the four Power 4 conference champions, and the highest-ranked Group of 6 team.

But the Power 4 conference championship games will be eliminated, with each league expected to determine its champion through regular-season standings and tiebreakers, according to ESPN. The Army-Navy game will take over the old conference championship weekend.

The expansion has drawn plenty of criticism. Nick Saban said that “there’s not 24 teams in the country that can win the national championship,” and that he hated to see games like the SEC Championship go away.

During a press conference on Tuesday, Drinkwitz was asked about the elimination of conference championship games, and he had a pretty interesting response as he questioned the point of competing in a conference if it’s not for a conference championship.

articles.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
articles.summary: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State, Dan Lanning announced on Monday.
body: “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.”

Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front.
In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game.

“I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.”

articles.title: Brilliant Noskova dismantles Gauff to reach WTA Finals last four
articles.summary: Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova dismantles Coco Gauff to become the first player to reach the last four at the WTA Finals.
body: Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova dismantled Coco Gauff to become the first player to reach the last four of the WTA Finals.
Czech Noskova played with controlled aggression and served brilliantly to beat the American 6-3 6-3.
World number eight Noskova was composed throughout and broke Gauff's serve four times in the first set alone.
She sent powerful winners to all corners to outmuscle her opponent, who is one of the best movers on the WTA Tour, and committed only one unforced error in a dominant second set.

articles.title: Vikings reportedly re-sign Cousins from Raiders
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have reportedly re-signed quarterback Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders in order to improve their offence.
body: Cousins spent six years with the Vikings from 2018-2023 before he left to join the Atlanta Falcons as a free agent in 2024.
The Vikings have since struggled to find a replacement for him and have eight quarterbacks start since his move.
It means that the 2026 No 1 pick Carlos Mendoza will now be the starting quarterback for the Raiders and the Las Vegas outfit have also received a 2027 third-round pick for the trade.
The Vikings had an extra third-round selection from Philadelphia in a swap they made in April for edge rusher Jonathan Greenard.
